name: get_guide
summary: How to use knitted well, a topic at a time: the numbers and habits that make work look designed, not merely generated. Read start first, then the topic before your first task of that kind. Topics: start, patterns, motion, voice, yarn, drawing, making, designing, knitting, brief, parts, posts, copywriting, organizing.

When the app on this computer was built after builtAt, an older copy is still running: ask the person to quit knitted and open it again.

name: apply_batch
summary: Apply several edit commands as ONE step, so a person can undo it as one. `atomic: true` applies all or nothing. Each command is {type, ...}: addStitch {stitch}, updateStitch {id, patch}, removeStitch {id}, reorder {id, toIndex}, setSize {size}, fillSlot {slot, content} (text slots only; set an image with updateStitch and a yarnId), setMeta {name, durationMs}, setMotion {stitchId, clips}, setAudio {audio}: the WHOLE list of sound clips, replacing what is there, so send every clip to keep (read them with get_pattern, motion.audio). A clip is {id, yarnId, startMs, kind: voice or music, gain (loudness: 1 as recorded, 0 silent, up to 2; every track is brought to one loudness first, so music sits well at 0.4 to 0.6, and the knit lowers it by itself while a voice speaks), fadeInMs, fadeOutMs, loop, label, fromMs (where in the file it starts playing, like a track's chorus at 30000; 0 if left out)}; any other field is refused. To change one clip's loudness, send the list with that clip's gain changed. setLocked is refused: only a person locks or unlocks.

params.description: One of text, media, motion, frame, cta, other.

params.name: folder
params.description: The folder the part goes in, as a path from the top of its section, like Royalty free music/Lo-fi. Made when it is not there. Left out, the top.

name: edit_part
summary: Change one of the project's own parts, or a library part, everywhere it is used. Returns the patternId the part is edited through: read and change it with the usual pattern tools (get_pattern, update_stitch, apply_batch and the rest), and every change goes to the part, as its next version. The pattern's frame is the part's own box, and its size is the part's shape. A stitch with a slot name is a slot of the part; a slot the brand locked stays locked. Patterns that use the part show the change at once and offer the person to accept it. The starter parts and parts written in code are not edited this way: duplicate a starter first.

params.name: partId
params.description: From list_parts

params.name: projectId
params.description: The project id, like pj_01...

name: list_presets
summary: The animation presets available to set_motion.

name: set_motion
summary: Animate a stitch: give it clips, each {preset, startMs, endMs}. Replaces that stitch's clips. Also set the pattern's length with durationMs if the animation runs past it. Keep text on screen long enough to read (about 3 words a second).

params.name: patternId
params.description: The pattern id, like pt_01...

params.name: stitch
params.description: Slot name or id

name: change_scene
summary: End one scene and start the next at a moment, as a video should, instead of covering the old scene with the new one while its words are still underneath. What leaves goes out a little apart, the last gone at atMs; what enters comes in from atMs, a little apart, top to bottom. leaving and entering are slot names or ids. A stitch's earlier exit (or entrance) is replaced, and its other clips are kept. Leave out what stays through both scenes, like a backdrop or a logo.

params.name: patternId
params.description: The pattern id, like pt_01...

params.name: atMs
params.description: The moment the next scene starts, in ms

params.name: leaving
params.description: What goes out: slot names or ids

params.name: entering
params.description: What comes in: slot names or ids

params.name: out
params.description: How it leaves; fade-out if left out. One of fade-out, slide-out-up, slide-out-down, slide-out-left, slide-out-right, shrink-out, wipe-out.

params.name: in
params.description: How it comes in; fade-in if left out. One of fade-in, slide-up, slide-down, slide-left, slide-right, pop, scale-in, stitch-in, type-on, wipe.

params.name: staggerMs
params.description: How far apart each one starts: 80 ms for exits and 150 ms for entrances if left out

name: list_voices
summary: What the configured voice can do: its voices, the model and its family, the style and other options set in Settings, and whether it works right now. Read it before synthesize_voiceover to pick a voice the server really has.

name: synthesize_voiceover
summary: Speak a script and put it on the pattern's timeline as sound, optionally with timed captions. Write it to be HEARD: never have the voice read a command, a file name, a path or code word for word (nobody follows 'filefreak sites rollback my-site 3' by ear); say what it does ('roll it back from the terminal') and leave the command on screen, or give that line as {say, show}. Give the WHOLE script in one call, a line per caption, never one call per line: it is spoken in one take, so the voice stays the same from start to end (a voice model asked line by line drifts in pitch and pace), then cut at the pauses into a clip per line, placed as spoken. Pick the voice from list_voices. style is how to say it, in words ("warm, confident, slower at the end"), for models that take one; options are any other fields the voice server takes. oneTake: false speaks each line on its own, only for lines that must stay separate. It waits until the voiceover is on the timeline and returns each line's clip and times (wait: false returns a job id at once). The pattern becomes a video long enough for the speech.

params.name: patternId
params.description: The pattern id, like pt_01...

params.name: lines
params.description: The whole script, in order: a line per caption. A string is said and shown; {say, show} when the screen should show other words, like a command

params.name: voice
params.description: A voice from list_voices

params.name: style
params.description: How to say it, in words, for models that take an instruction

params.name: options
params.description: Other fields for the voice server, as it documents them

params.name: oneTake
params.description: Default true: one take, cut into lines

params.name: wait
params.description: Default true: wait until it is spoken and placed, and return the clips and their times

name: preview_pattern
summary: Render the pattern and SEE it: returns a PNG. Use it after layout changes to check your own work. `time` is milliseconds for animated patterns.

params.name: patternId
params.description: The pattern id, like pt_01...

name: check_pattern
summary: Run the same quality checks Knit runs, without drawing anything: missing files, low contrast, text that will not fit, animation that is too busy. Fix errors before knitting.

params.name: patternId
params.description: The pattern id, like pt_01...

name: check_claims
summary: Before words are knitted or posted, read a pattern's words beside its project's Brief, to check each claim: what the business does, works with or costs, what it has done or will do, numbers, names and quotes. Give each claim one of four answers: backed (the Brief says it), against (the Brief says otherwise), not yet (the Brief says planned, in beta or by invitation, and the words say it as if anyone can have it now), or not in the Brief (nothing backs it: it may be a gap in the Brief, so ask the person). Change what is against or not yet to what the Brief says, and tell the person what you changed and what is not in the Brief.

params.name: patternId
params.description: The pattern id, like pt_01...

name: knit_pattern
summary: Make real files (PNG, JPEG, WebP or MP4) from a pattern, through the same job the studio's Knit button uses, with the same checks. `params`: sizes (array of {name,w,h}), format, scale (1 or 2), fps (30, or 60 for smoother fast motion, which takes about twice as long), rows (an array of objects of slot values, one per post, to make many). A row may only fill free slots. Returns file paths and any issues, or a jobId when wait is false.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The project id, like pj_01...

params.name: patternId
params.description: The pattern id, like pt_01...

name: get_job
summary: Check on a job: a knit, a voiceover, pictures of a website, or photos or a video being made. Give waitSeconds to wait for it to finish, rather than calling again and again: every call re-reads the whole conversation, which costs the person.

params.name: jobId
params.description: From knit_pattern, synthesize_voiceover or capture_website

params.name: waitSeconds
params.description: Wait up to this long for it to finish before answering

name: cancel_job
summary: Stop a running job.

params.name: jobId
params.description: The job id

name: list_knits
summary: What has been knitted in a project, newest first, a page at a time: total says how many there are, so page on with offset. Each knit (a pattern at one size) is listed once, as the file the person sees for it in Knits: knitting it again after a change makes a new version of it, not another knit, and versions says how many it has; otherFormats are the same picture as another file type or scale. everyVersion lists every file instead. A knit with patternChangedSince was made before its pattern was last saved, so it may not show the pattern as it is now: knit it again before it is posted.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The project. Not needed with patternId

params.name: folder
params.description: Only knits in this folder and the folders inside it

params.name: patternId
params.description: Only knits of this pattern

params.name: favorite
params.description: Only the person's favourites: what they liked best, the surest guide to what they want more of

params.name: kind
params.description: Only pictures, or only videos. One of image, video.

params.name: size
params.description: Only knits of this shape, at any scale: Story is 9:16 (Stories, Reels, TikTok, Shorts), Post 4:5, Square 1:1, Landscape 16:9 (YouTube), Banner; Other for any other shape. One of Story, Post, Square, Landscape, Banner, Other.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many, 30 if left out

params.name: offset
params.description: How many of the newest to skip

params.name: everyVersion
params.description: Every file: each version and format of each knit, not only the one shown for it

name: tag_knit
summary: Set the tags on a knit: words to find it by in Knits, like launch or winter. Replaces the tags it has, so send every tag to keep.

params.name: knitId
params.description: The knit, by its id from list_knits

name: favorite_knit
summary: Mark knits as the person's favourites, or take them off, as the star in Knits does. Do it when the person asks: favourites are their own picks.

params.name: knitIds
params.description: The knits, by id from list_knits

params.name: favorite
params.description: true to mark them, false to take them off

name: set_knit_post
summary: Save what goes with a knit when it is posted: its caption, hashtags, and a track from the project's audio Yarn with a sentence on why it suits. What you leave out stays as it is. The person sees it in Knits, and can edit it. Read the guide topic posts first.

params.name: knitId
params.description: The knit, by its id from list_knits

params.name: caption
params.description: The words, the hook first

params.name: hashtags
params.description: Each with or without its #

params.name: audioId
params.description: A Yarn id of kind audio from this project, or an empty string for no track

params.name: audioWhy
params.description: Why that track suits it, in a sentence

name: list_social_accounts
summary: The person's social accounts knitted can post to (connected in Settings, Social), each with what its platform takes, and whether you may schedule posts or only make drafts. An account with status reconnect cannot post until the person connects it again.

name: schedule_post
summary: Post knits to the person's accounts: one post per account, of one knit, or several as a carousel. With `at`, at that time; without, as soon as it can. Unless the person lets you schedule (list_social_accounts says), these are drafts for them to schedule. Each platform's limits are checked first and every refusal is said, so fix and send again. Write the caption with the guide topics posts and copywriting: the caption as posted, hashtags in it. TikTok needs options.tiktok.privacy, one of the account's choices, which only the person should pick: leave TikTok to them unless they told you which. YouTube needs a title.

params.name: knitIds
params.description: The knits, by id from list_knits, in the order they are shown. One video, or pictures

params.name: accountIds
params.description: The accounts, by id from list_social_accounts

params.name: caption
params.description: The words as posted, hashtags included

params.name: captions
params.description: A caption for one platform instead, by platform: {"x": "shorter"}

params.name: title
params.description: YouTube's title, up to 100 characters

params.name: at
params.description: When, as an ISO time with its offset, like 2026-11-20T09:00:00-05:00. Left out, now

params.name: draft
params.description: true to make drafts even if you may schedule

params.name: options
params.description: Each platform's own choices, by platform: tiktok {privacy, comments, duet, stitch}, youtube {privacy: public, unlisted or private, madeForKids}, linkedin {visibility: PUBLIC or CONNECTIONS}, instagram {shareToFeed}

name: list_posts
summary: A project's posts, newest first: drafts, scheduled, posted (with a link), failed and missed (with why). Give status to see only some.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The project id, like pj_01...

name: post_insights
summary: How the person's posts did, and what did better, from their own numbers: each platform's totals, findings like 'Videos got 1.8 times your usual views (6 posts)' that need 3 posts on each side, and each post against the usual for its account about a week in. Read it before planning posts or writing captions for an account that has posted before. Leave out projectId for every project.

params.name: projectId
params.description: One project, by id; left out, all of them

name: cancel_post
summary: Stop a draft or scheduled post from going out. One already posted stays on its platform.

params.name: postId
params.description: The post, by id from list_posts

name: list_designs
summary: A project's design sheets: whole sites on one board, like a Figma file, in labelled sections of frames. Each frame is a screen or a piece of one, in HTML and CSS.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The project id, like pj_01...

name: get_design
summary: Read a design sheet: its sections and frames by id. Give frameId for that frame's HTML and CSS, or code: true for every frame's. Look at it with view_design.

params.name: designId
params.description: The design id, like ds_01...

params.name: frameId
params.description: A frame's id, like f7, for its code

params.name: code
params.description: Every frame's HTML and CSS. A sheet's code can be long: ask for one frame when that is enough.

name: create_design
summary: START a design sheet for a whole site. start "brand" (the default) begins with Foundations (colours, type, buttons and fields), Components (header, footer) and Pages (a home page on desktop and mobile), all drawn with the brand's Swatch, to make into the business's own; "blank" begins with one empty Pages section. Then design with set_design_frame. Read get_guide designing first.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The project id, like pj_01...

params.name: name
params.description: Like "Website" or "Spring launch page"

params.name: start
params.description: One of brand, blank.

name: set_design_frame
summary: DESIGN one frame of a sheet: a page, a screen or a piece of one, as HTML and CSS, and SEE it. Give frameId to change one, or leave it out to add one to the section (by id or name; a section that is not there yet is added). The brand is in CSS variables: var(--color-primary) and the other roles, var(--color-on-primary) for text on it, var(--font-display), var(--font-body), var(--radius). Pictures from Yarn are yarn:<id>, the logo yarn:logo. No scripts, and nothing from the web. It comes back drawn: look, and fix what is off.

params.name: designId
params.description: The design id, like ds_01...

params.name: section
params.description: The section's id or name, like s3 or "Pages"

params.name: frameId
params.description: The frame to change, like f7. Leave out to add a frame

params.name: name
params.description: Like "Home" or "Pricing, mobile"

params.name: device
params.description: desktop is 1440 wide, tablet 834, mobile 390. Or give width.. One of desktop, tablet, mobile.

params.name: width
params.description: In pixels, 240 to 3840, when not a device's

params.name: height
params.description: A fixed height, like one phone screen (844). Leave it out to keep the height it has; 0 for a frame as tall as what is in it.

params.name: html
params.description: The frame's body, without <html>, <head> or <body>

params.name: css
params.description: Its styles. They are its own: no other frame sees them

params.name: note
params.description: What it is for, or what is still to do

name: arrange_design
summary: ARRANGE a design sheet, all changes or none: rename it, add, rename, move or remove sections, and move, copy or remove frames. Each change is { op, ... }: rename {name}; addSection {name, note?, at?}; updateSection {section, name?, note?}; moveSection {section, to}; removeSection {section}; moveFrame {frameId, section, at?}; duplicateFrame {frameId, name?}; removeFrame {frameId}. at and to count from 0. The person can undo it.

params.name: designId
params.description: The design id, like ds_01...

name: view_design
summary: LOOK at a design sheet as the person sees it: the whole board with its labelled sections, one section, or one frame. A whole sheet is small: look at a frame or a section to check the detail. A tall frame is cut into columns, left to right.

params.name: designId
params.description: The design id, like ds_01...

params.name: sectionId
params.description: A section's id or name, for just that section

params.name: frameId
params.description: A frame's id, for just that frame

name: list_comments
summary: The person's comments: notes pinned to a spot on a knit (and a moment, in a video) or on a frame of a design sheet, saying what to change there. Each says where it is and what is under it can be seen with view_comment. Open ones only, unless open is false. Look at one with view_comment before you change anything, and answer it with reply_comment when it is done.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The project id, like pj_01...

params.name: knitId
params.description: A knit's id, for its comments

params.name: designId
params.description: The design id, like ds_01...

params.name: frameId
params.description: With designId, one frame's comments

params.name: open
params.description: Only those not resolved yet. True unless said.

name: view_comment
summary: LOOK at a comment: the knit (at the comment's moment, in a video) or the frame, with the pin drawn where the person put it, beside a close-up of that spot. Says what is under the pin (the stitch in the knit's pattern, or the element in the frame's HTML), the whole thread, and how to change that part.

params.name: commentId
params.description: The comment's id, like cm_01...

name: reply_comment
summary: Answer a comment: say what you changed, or ask what the person meant. resolve: true when the change is made and knitted again (or saved, on a design), so it leaves the open list; the person can open it again.

params.name: commentId
params.description: The comment's id, like cm_01...

params.name: text
params.description: What you did, or your question, in plain words

params.name: resolve
params.description: True when it is done

name: list_folders
summary: How a project's things are sorted: each section (patterns, yarn, parts, swatches, knits, reference) has folders of its own, which can hold folders. Each folder is a path like Royalty free music/Lo-fi, with how many things are in it, not counting the folders inside. Give a section for just that one.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The project id, like pj_01...

params.name: section
params.description: Which section the folder is in: each of patterns, yarn, parts, swatches, knits and reference (the Brief's files) has folders of its own. One of patterns, yarn, parts, swatches, knits, reference.

name: move_to_folder
summary: File things into a folder, to sort a project the way its person thinks of it: one folder per campaign, a folder for royalty free music with one inside for each kind. Give the folder as a path, like Royalty free music/Lo-fi, or "" for the top; it is made when it is not there, in each section the things are from. Give the ids of what to move, of one kind or several. Moving changes nothing else about them. With no ids, give a section, and the folder is made there, empty, ready to fill. To move or rename a folder itself, use rename.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The project id, like pj_01...

params.name: folder
params.description: The folder's path, like Royalty free music/Lo-fi, or "" for the top

params.name: yarnIds
params.description: The ids of the Yarn to move

params.name: patternIds
params.description: The ids of the patterns to move

params.name: partIds
params.description: The ids of the parts (not the starter parts) to move

params.name: swatchIds
params.description: The ids of the swatches to move

params.name: knitIds
params.description: The ids of the knits to move

params.name: referenceIds
params.description: The ids of the reference files: moving a file from Yarn here puts it in the reference, and back to move

params.name: section
params.description: With no ids, the section to make the folder in, empty. One of patterns, yarn, parts, swatches, knits, reference.
